Every tool the omniglass MCP server serves, generated from the [API](/reference/api/) by the same
`make gen` that generates the CLI. A tool is an API operation stamped for MCP in the server's Go
source: calling it runs that route with the caller's token, so its gate, its scope and its audit row
are the route's own, and the row records that it came over MCP. To connect an agent, see
[connect an agent](/guides/agents/).

Each tool says what a client may assume of it, from one rule over the route's method and gate:

- **read-only**: changes nothing (a read, or a preview gated by a read). A client may run it freely.
- **destructive**: overwrites or removes something, or acts on a component. A client should confirm it with
  its user.
- **idempotent**: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more.
- **open-world**: reaches outside omniglass.

A tool that is not read-only and not destructive adds something (a create).

51 tools.

## `get-auth-me`

The authenticated principal, its permissions, and grants

Returns the caller's principal, flattened permissions (a UI hint and the fast-reject set), the permissions held on an all-scope grant (fleet_permissions), and grants. Requires authentication.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/auth/me`
- Gate: authn only
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `list-component-types`

List component types

Lists the component_type registry (the taxonomy a product is classified under: mic, camera, wireless-mic under mic), ordered alphabetically by label. Each row carries its parent link, so the console reconstructs the tree client-side. Gated by component_type:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/component-types`
- Gate: `component_type:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `list-components`

List components in scope

Lists the components the caller may read, each filtered to its scope subtree. Gated by component:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/components`
- Gate: `component:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `create-component`

Create a component

Creates a component, optionally under a parent (a root needs an all-scoped grant), bound to a system and a location, and classified by a product (required; naming a generic is fine until a real product is modeled). Gated by component:create. The location reference resolves within the caller's location:read scope, because the label this stores is rendered from it, and one outside that scope is refused (422) exactly as :renderLabel refuses to preview it. Naming a system additionally requires system:update, and resolves within that scope, because the component's primary membership is inserted from it: it is the same row the membership route writes, so the two paths cost the same permission. A system outside that scope is refused with a 403 naming it when the caller may read the system (denying its existence to someone who can GET it would be a lie) and with the non-disclosing 422 when the caller may not.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/components`
- Gate: `component:create`
- Assume: adds

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expected_name` | string | no | The name a create form previewed (POST /components:renderLabel returns it). The create is refused with a 409 naming what it would produce instead, rather than silently landing a different name, if the number was taken or the type's stem moved while the form was open. It does not name the row (the platform still does, and the row is still name_generated): it only asserts what that name will be. Applies only when the platform names the row: sending it beside a name is a 422. |
| `label` | string | no | What an operator reads; the name is the address |
| `location` | string | no | Location name this component is placed at |
| `name` | string | no | Name, unique within its placement (the address; lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Omit to have the platform generate one from the product's type. |
| `parent` | string | no | Parent component name; omit for a root component |
| `product` | string | no | Product (catalog SKU) this component is an instance of, by name or uuid. Required: use a generic (generic-device, generic-app, generic-service) until a real product is modeled. |
| `system` | string | no | Primary system name this component belongs to. Naming one writes that system's membership, so it costs the system:update permission and resolves in that scope; omitted, the create costs component:create alone. |

## `list-component-alarms`

List a component's alarms

What is currently wrong with this component, newest first, with the component's own verdict those alarms make. Pass include_cleared for the history rather than the active set. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/components/{name}/alarms`
- Gate: `component:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_cleared` | boolean | no | Include cleared alarms, so the list is the history rather than what is wrong now |
| `name` | string | yes | The component's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a.$comp.display-1) |
| `unacknowledged` | boolean | no | Only the alarms nobody has looked at. On its own this is the queue an operator works (raised and unacknowledged); with include_cleared it also returns the incidents that came and went unattended |

## `list-component-commands`

List a component's commands

The component's command history, newest first, each command whole (as the single read returns it), narrowed by recorded status and by when it was issued, a page at a time. status=issued is what is in flight now. Gated by command:read, resolved on the component tier; a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but whose commands it may not is a 403.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/components/{name}/commands`
- Gate: `command:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | no | How many to return, newest first (1 to 500) |
| `name` | string | yes | The component's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a.$comp.display-1) |
| `since` | string | no | Only the commands issued at or after this RFC3339 time |
| `status` | string | no | Only the commands with this recorded status; issued is every command still in flight |
| `until` | string | no | Only the commands issued at or before this RFC3339 time |

## `get-component-command`

Read a command

One command, whole: what it was told and the value it set, its recorded status with a time for each transition (issued, delivered, executed, settled), where it sits now while in flight (queued, delivered, awaiting the reply, awaiting the observation), how its binding settles it, the evidence that decided it (the reply, masked of credentials, or the observed sample) and why, the endpoint, node and driver that carry it, and who issued it. Gated by command:read, resolved on the component tier; a component outside the caller's component:read, or a command not on that component, is a non-disclosing 404, and a component it can read but whose commands it may not is a 403.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/components/{name}/commands/{id}`
- Gate: `command:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes | The command's id, as its issue answered it |
| `name` | string | yes | The component's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a.$comp.display-1) |

## `issue-component-command`

Issue a command to a component

Records a command invocation, writes a caused event, and (for a settleable command) opens an intended value the observed value settles against. Answers with the command as it stands (as the command read returns it) and the computed settlement verdict; with wait, once it settles, fails or times out, or wait_timeout passes. Gated by command:issue, whose scope is resolved on the component tier from that permission (not from component:read); a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but not command is a 403.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/components/{name}/commands:issue`
- Gate: `command:issue`
- Assume: destructive, open-world

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command_type` | string | yes | The command_type to invoke |
| `instance` | string | no | The series discriminator (e.g. an endpoint), when the target is instanced |
| `name` | string | yes | The component's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a.$comp.display-1) |
| `params` | any | no | The invocation params, stored on the command and the caused event |
| `value` | any | no | The intended value for the target property (a settleable command) |
| `wait` | boolean | no | Block until the command settles, fails or times out, or until wait_timeout passes, and answer with where it stands then. Refused with a 429, before anything is issued, while too many commands are already being waited on |
| `wait_timeout` | integer | no | How long a wait may block, in seconds (1 to 120). A command still in flight when it passes is answered as it stands, its phase saying where |

## `list-component-logs`

List a component's recent log lines

Returns the component's recent raw log lines (the ingest lane of ADR-0066, distinct from typed events), newest first, bounded to the last 24 hours, narrowed by an optional severity threshold and source, with the sources the window carries. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/components/{name}/logs`
- Gate: `component:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| `name` | string | yes | The component's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a.$comp.display-1) |
| `severity` | string | no | Only lines at this severity or more severe (RFC 5424's eight levels); a line with no severity is left out |
| `source` | string | no | Only lines that arrived on this channel |

## `get-component-reconciliation`

Read a component's property reconciliation (want/told/is)

Pivots, per declared property, the declared value (want, resolved live from the cascade), the intended value (told), and the observed value (is, resolved across every live instance of the property and naming the instance it came from; a deleted endpoint's frozen reading is left out), with config-drift computed on read: drift when any live observed instance differs from want. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/components/{name}/reconciliation`
- Gate: `component:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The component's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a.$comp.display-1) |

## `preview-driver`

Preview a driver spec's polls through a node

Runs a driver spec's polls once through the node named, against the target its inputs name, and answers with what each poll read: the samples its emits extracted, each emit that did not locate, and an excerpt of the raw answer, masked of every secret the preview used. Nothing is stored. The spec is a stored driver (driver) or an unsaved one (spec); an invalid spec is a 422 listing its findings, as validate-driver-spec gives them. A preview runs a poll that is its own request (http, https, an snmp get, a tcp line); a poll that rides a held session or a bound socket needs an attached endpoint (run-endpoint-poll). A secret input must be one the caller may reveal (secret:reveal), since the preview hands it to the target named. A node that is not connected is a 503, one that does not answer in time a 504; too many runs in flight is a 429. Audited on the node and on each secret used. Gated by driver:preview.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/drivers:preview`
- Gate: `driver:preview`
- Assume: destructive, open-world

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `driver` | string | no | A stored driver to preview, by name; or give spec |
| `inputs` | object | no | The inputs an attach would take (host, port, a secret by name); a secret must be one you may reveal, since a preview hands it to the target |
| `node` | string | yes | The node that runs the preview, by name: the one that reaches the target |
| `polls` | array | no | The polls to run, by name; absent runs every poll |
| `spec` | any | no | A driver spec to preview inline, unsaved; or give driver |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | no | How long the node may take for the whole preview (default 15, at most 30) |

## `validate-driver-spec`

Check a driver spec without saving it

Checks a driver spec by the rules a save applies (the strict parse, then validation against the live catalogs) and writes nothing. The answer lists every fault the validator can pin down, each pinned on the function it is in, the first always the fault a save would name; an empty list is a spec create-driver accepts. Gated by driver:read.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/drivers:validate`
- Gate: `driver:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | any | yes | The driver spec to check, as create-driver takes it |

Lists the endpoints whose owning component the caller may read (the component cascade). Gated by endpoint:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/endpoints`
- Gate: `endpoint:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `create-endpoint`

Create an endpoint

Creates an endpoint owned by a component (or a server-hosted one, which needs an all-scoped grant), named by its transport; the optional label is the only identity string an operator types, and is where what the connection is FOR goes. The create scope cascades through the owning component. Gated by endpoint:create.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/endpoints`
- Gate: `endpoint:create`
- Assume: open-world

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component` | string | no | Owning component, by name or id; omit for a server-hosted endpoint (needs an all-scoped grant) |
| `driver` | string | no | Attach this driver (by name or id): the spec derives the transport and params, and the endpoint's tasks derive from the spec's functions |
| `inputs` | object | no | The inputs the driver's spec declares (host, port, credentials as secret reference names); required ones must be supplied, defaults fill the rest |
| `label` | string | no | What an operator reads in lists (Control processor). Settable here because the name is derived from the transport, so it says how the device is reached and never what the connection is for |
| `node` | string | no | Node placement, by name or id |
| `params` | any | no | Address/target settings (jsonb); an attach derives them from the inputs instead |
| `transport` | string | no | A transport name from the code registry (GET /transports); the endpoint is named by it, unique within the component. Exactly one of transport (a bare probe endpoint) or driver (an attach) is set |

## `get-endpoint`

Get an endpoint

Fetches an endpoint by its address (<component>/<endpoint name>) or uuid. An endpoint whose component is out of the caller's read scope is a non-disclosing 404, and a name no endpoint the caller can see answers to is a 404 naming what was looked up (listing each match when more than one does). Gated by endpoint:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/endpoints/{endpoint}`
- Gate: `endpoint:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | The endpoint, as <component>/<endpoint name> (the component by name, dotted address or uuid) or by its uuid. The slash is percent-encoded in a URL, as the CLI does |

## `update-endpoint`

Update an endpoint

Patches an endpoint's node placement, params, label, or (driver-attached) its connection inputs in place: the host, port and attached secret references, validated against the driver's declared inputs, the endpoint's tasks re-derived in the same transaction. A value the driver refuses is a 400 naming the field. An empty label clears it and the surface falls back to the derived name. Gated by endpoint:update; read and update scopes (through the component) drive the 404 versus 403 split.

- Route: `PATCH /api/v1/endpoints/{endpoint}`
- Gate: `endpoint:update`
- Assume: destructive, open-world

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | The endpoint, as <component>/<endpoint name> (the component by name, dotted address or uuid) or by its uuid. The slash is percent-encoded in a URL, as the CLI does |
| `inputs` | object | no | A driver-attached endpoint's inputs, edited in place (#1061): the host, the port, an attached secret's reference name, any input the driver declares. Merged over the stored inputs and validated against the driver; a value it refuses is a 400 naming the input. Changing where a credential is sent needs the caller to be able to use that credential |
| `label` | string | no | A new label; an empty string clears it, and the surface falls back to the derived name. Omit to leave it alone |
| `node` | string | no | Reassign the node placement, by name or id |
| `params` | any | no | Replace the address/target settings (jsonb). On a driver-attached endpoint only the timeout is set here: its address derives from its host and port inputs |
| `transport` | string | no | The transport: a driver-attached endpoint takes only one its driver speaks |

## `delete-endpoint`

Delete an endpoint

Deletes an endpoint, refused while a task still references it. Gated by endpoint:delete; read and delete scopes (through the component) drive the 404 versus 403 split.

- Route: `DELETE /api/v1/endpoints/{endpoint}`
- Gate: `endpoint:delete`
- Assume: destructive, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | The endpoint, as <component>/<endpoint name> (the component by name, dotted address or uuid) or by its uuid. The slash is percent-encoded in a URL, as the CLI does |

## `run-endpoint-poll`

Run an endpoint's poll now

Runs one of an attached endpoint's polls now, on the node that holds the endpoint, outside its schedule (which is unchanged), and answers with what it read. The samples land as a scheduled run's do. The run borrows the endpoint's held session where it has one and honors its gate: a gated endpoint refuses the run with the gate's reason (409) and nothing is sent. A poll the endpoint does not have is a 404 naming the polls it has; an endpoint on no node is a 409. A node that is not connected is a 503, one that does not answer in time a 504; too many runs in flight is a 429. Audited on the endpoint. Gated by endpoint:run; read and run scopes (through the component) drive the 404 versus 403 split.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/endpoints/{endpoint}/polls/{poll}:run`
- Gate: `endpoint:run`
- Assume: open-world

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | The endpoint, as <component>/<endpoint name> or its id |
| `poll` | string | yes | The poll to run, by its function name |
| `timeout_seconds` | integer | no | How long the node may take (default 15, at most 30) |

## `retry-endpoint`

Retry an endpoint's gated connections

Moves the endpoint's retry counter, which is part of its connection fingerprint: a gate a refusal retrying cannot fix holds (a wrong credential, a changed host key or certificate, a reply its driver declares terminal) lifts, the node recycles the endpoint's held session, and every connection to it is attempted again. Fixing the secret, the address, the transport, the tls mode or the driver's login needs no retry: the change moves the fingerprint itself. An unrelated edit (a label) moves nothing. host_key names a key to trust, the one the endpoint's transport pins (the offered key a key refusal names): an ssh host key, or a tls or https endpoint's certificate public key, which such an endpoint also takes as certificate. It becomes the declared pin and recycles the session onto it whatever its state, an audited acceptance of the change. While the endpoint's gate names an offered key, the key must be that key, so a trust confirmed against a refusal the record has since moved past is a 409 and changes nothing. Audited, a trusted key with the pin it replaced (old) and the pin it set (new). Gated by endpoint:retry; read and retry scopes (through the component) drive the 404 versus 403 split.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/endpoints/{endpoint}:retry`
- Gate: `endpoint:retry`
- Assume: destructive, open-world

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `certificate` | string | no | A tls or https endpoint only: the same as host_key, named for the certificate (the offered_key a certificate refusal names). It becomes the endpoint's declared tls-certificate pin, held to the same rule (the exact offered key while a key refusal holds), and the session redials onto it. Omit to retry with the pin unchanged |
| `endpoint` | string | yes | The endpoint, as <component>/<endpoint name> (the component by name, dotted address or uuid) or by its uuid. The slash is percent-encoded in a URL, as the CLI does |
| `host_key` | string | no | The SHA256 fingerprint of a changed key the operator now trusts, the key the endpoint's transport pins (the offered_key a key refusal names on the component's reachability read): an ssh endpoint's host key, which becomes its declared ssh-host-key, or a tls or https endpoint's certificate public key, which becomes its declared tls-certificate. The session redials onto it. While a key refusal holds, it must be that exact offered key: any other is a 409 that changes nothing (the refusal on record is the node's last word, so to trust a key the component presents since, retry without a key first). With no key refusal held it declares a pin ahead of time. Omit to retry with the pin unchanged |

## `rotate-endpoint-token`

Rotate a webhook endpoint's token

Mints a webhook endpoint's token anew (#1024): a post bearing the old one answers 404 at once, exactly as a token that never existed, and the new one is revealed through the endpoint's secret, to give the sender. A token deleted with its secret is minted again. A dialed endpoint has no token, a 422. Audited on the endpoint and the secret. Gated by endpoint:update; read and update scopes (through the component) drive the 404 versus 403 split.

- Route: `POST /api/v1/endpoints/{endpoint}:rotateToken`
- Gate: `endpoint:update`
- Assume: destructive

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | The endpoint, as <component>/<endpoint name> (the component by name, dotted address or uuid) or by its uuid. The slash is percent-encoded in a URL, as the CLI does |

## `list-locations`

List locations in scope

Lists the locations the caller may read, each filtered to its scope subtree. Gated by location:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/locations`
- Gate: `location:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `get-location`

Get a location

Fetches a location by name within the caller's read scope. Out of scope is a non-disclosing 404. Gated by location:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/locations/{name}`
- Gate: `location:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The location's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a) |

## `get-location-health`

Read a location's health

The location's current verdict, worst-wins over every system placed anywhere beneath it, with those systems and their verdicts as the drill-down (the system health read names the role, which occupant is down, and the alarm). Transitions are the recorded edges over the last 30 days. Gated by location:read; an out-of-scope location is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/locations/{name}/health`
- Gate: `location:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The location's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.415a) |

## `list-nodes`

List nodes

Lists the edge nodes. A node is fleet-wide, so listing requires an all-scope read. Gated by node:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/nodes`
- Gate: `node:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `get-node`

Get a node

Fetches a node by name. Requires an all-scope read. Gated by node:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/nodes/{name}`
- Gate: `node:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The node's unique name |

## `list-node-logs`

List a node's recent self-logs

Returns the node's own recent operational log lines (the raw ingest lane of ADR-0066, owner-bound to the node), newest first, bounded to the last 24 hours. Gated by node:read; an out-of-scope node is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/nodes/{name}/logs`
- Gate: `node:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The node's unique name |

## `list-products`

List products

Lists the product registry, ordered alphabetically by label. Each product carries its vendor, driver, kind, and component_type. Gated by product:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/products`
- Gate: `product:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `get-product`

Get a product

Fetches a product by its name or its uuid. Either form resolves, so `omniglass product get acme-soundbar` and the uuid are interchangeable. Gated by product:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/products/{id}`
- Gate: `product:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The product, by name or uuid |

## `list-secret-types`

List secret types

Lists the secret_type shapes a secret can take, for the create form. Gated by secret:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/secret-types`
- Gate: `secret:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `list-secrets`

List secrets

Lists the secrets the caller may see, with masked fields, filtered to the read scope; admin-sensitive secrets appear only to the admin tier. Gated by secret:read, which the viewer floor does not carry (secret is a sensitive resource).

- Route: `GET /api/v1/secrets`
- Gate: `secret:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `create-secret`

Create a secret

Seals a secret at an owner scope. Fields are validated and encrypted against the type shape. Gated by secret:create, plus platform:create when owner_kind is platform (the install-wide tier).

- Route: `POST /api/v1/secrets`
- Gate: `secret:create`
- Assume: adds

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admin_sensitive` | boolean | no | Admin-only visibility; omit to use the type default. Setting true requires the admin tier |
| `fields` | object | yes | The operator field map, validated against the type shape |
| `label` | string | no | What an operator reads in lists and pickers (Polling community); omit to fall back to the name |
| `name` | string | yes | The cascade name (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens); unique per owner |
| `owner` | string | no | The owning entity's name; omit for a platform secret |
| `owner_kind` | string | yes | Which tier owns this secret (the system band is retired, ADR-0052) |
| `secret_type` | string | yes | A secret_type id |

## `list-systems`

List systems in scope

Lists the systems the caller may read, each filtered to its scope subtree. Gated by system:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/systems`
- Gate: `system:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `get-system`

Get a system

Fetches a system by name within the caller's read scope. Out of scope is a non-disclosing 404. Gated by system:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/systems/{name}`
- Gate: `system:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The system's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.$sys.av) |

## `get-system-health`

Read a system's health

The system's current verdict and why: every role it needs filled, whether it is impaired, what an impaired role means for the system (impact), and for an impaired role which assigned components are down plus the alarms that took them down. A role that belongs to a choice (#626, an exclusive-or group such as an all-in-one alternate versus a component-built one) carries choice and alternate, and active is false when a different alternate answered the choice, meaning this role's own impaired figure did not move the verdict. Transitions are the recorded edges over the last 30 days, one entry per change. Gated by system:read; an out-of-scope system is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/systems/{name}/health`
- Gate: `system:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The system's name, or a dotted address (e.g. boi.17c.$sys.av) |

## `list-system-metric-series`

Read one metric series' raw samples

The samples behind the effective read's latest value for one series, newest first, windowed (hours) and capped (limit, newest kept). Gated by system:read; an out-of-scope owner is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/systems/{name}/metrics/{metric}/samples`
- Gate: `system:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hours` | integer | no | The window in hours, counted back from now; 24 when unset |
| `limit` | integer | no | The row cap, newest kept; 500 when unset |
| `metric` | string | yes | The metric_type name of the series |
| `name` | string | yes | The owner's name or uuid |

## `list-system-property-series`

Read one property series' change history

The change history behind the effective value for one property series, newest first, windowed (hours) and capped (limit, newest kept). Gated by system:read; an out-of-scope owner is a non-disclosing 404.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/systems/{name}/properties/{property}/samples`
- Gate: `system:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hours` | integer | no | The window in hours, counted back from now; 24 when unset |
| `limit` | integer | no | The row cap, newest kept; 500 when unset |
| `name` | string | yes | The owner's name or uuid |
| `property` | string | yes | The property_type name of the series |

## `list-tasks`

List tasks in scope

Lists the tasks whose endpoint's owning component the caller may read (the component cascade). Tasks are derived from endpoints, not authored. Gated by task:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/tasks`
- Gate: `task:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `list-transports`

List the transports the platform speaks

Lists the transport registry: the wires an endpoint can speak over, a build-time fact of the binary (ADR-0073). Gated by endpoint:read, the surface that consumes it.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/transports`
- Gate: `endpoint:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `list-unclaimed-sources`

List the sources no endpoint claims

The unclaimed-source inbox: each source a listener heard from that no endpoint claims (a webhook post to an unknown or rotated token), with how often, when first and last, and its last message cut to 512 bytes. Bounded at 256 sources per listener, the least recently heard evicted, and aged out after seven days; a source is let go once its messages land on an endpoint. Claim one by creating its endpoint. Gated by node:read on an all-scope grant: it is the listener's own observation, and listeners are fleet-wide as nodes are.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/unclaimed-sources`
- Gate: `node:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none

## `list-vendors`

List vendors

Lists the vendor registry, ordered alphabetically by label. Populates the vendor picker on the product form. Gated by vendor:read.

- Route: `GET /api/v1/vendors`
- Gate: `vendor:read`
- Assume: read-only, idempotent
- Arguments: none
